game: LV@DEN Week 10 2025, kickoff 2025-11-06 20:15 ET, DEN -9.5, total 42.5, outdoors (forecast not saved). Read as of morning of kickoff, pack only.

script.base: Denver leads by about a score to two scores at home (implied 26.0-16.5 on a 42.5 total, not a shootout). Nix does not have to chase, and the lead back, Dobbins (44 carries, 253 yards in weeks 7-9), gets the late carries against a LV run defense that allows 4.02 YPC and 22 runs of 10+ in 8 games. Las Vegas, a 9.5 dog, gets off designed runs; Jeanty's recent 14-carry, 3.29 YPC role shrinks, and Denver has allowed only nine 10-yard runs in nine games.
script.flip1: Geno Smith (already the L3 rusher, 8/10; O'Connell is out, so this is continuity not a new QB) keeps LV within a score, helped by Surtain being out. LV never abandons Jeanty — he had 67 and 75 rush yards in the older half of his last four — and Denver stays pass-heavy enough that Dobbins does not get a clock-killing fourth quarter.
script.flip2: Denver jumps up by 21+ early. Dobbins and the starters sit, and Harvey (13 carries in three games, and a 46-yard rush game in the last four) closes it, capping Dobbins under 79.5. LV empties the playbook through the air, so Jeanty's rush line dies even harder while Mayer, Bowers and Tucker pile up garbage receiving yards.

matchup.pressure: DEN blitzes 32% and LV is worse when blitzed (EPA/db -0.15 vs blitz, 0.00 vs none), so LV should be off schedule with more checkdowns and fewer clean deep shots. LV blitzes only 22%; DEN is better when blitzed (EPA/db +0.22 vs blitz, +0.05 vs none), so Nix is not forced off the run or the deep shot.
matchup.bleeds: DEN does not bleed the run: 3.70 YPC, 9 runs of 10+ in 9 games, 21 passes of 20+ for 337 yards. DEN does bleed the middle and the right side of the pass defense, and locks the left. LV bleeds the run (4.02 YPC, 22 runs of 10+ in 8 games) and the left/middle pass (21 passes of 20+ for 283).
matchup.overlap: LV's live usage is the middle: Mayer 16 targets/86 yards, Bowers 13/127, Jeanty 10/71 receiving, Tucker 15/141 on only 46 air yards. That overlaps DEN's middle YPA hole and the blitz-checkdown funnel, but Surtain's absence makes the 9-game pass splits stale, and receptions are not an available market. The rush overlap that is actually in the numbers is the inverse one: Jeanty into a front that does not bleed, and Dobbins into a LV front that does. Franklin's 476 air yards overlap LV's soft left side only if Denver is throwing, which the base script does not require.

pre_mortem: It's the morning after and the Jeanty under lost because the game stayed one score, LV gave him 18-plus carries, and he broke one of the few 10-yard runs Denver allows, finishing in the 67-75 range he already showed twice in the last four. The Dobbins over lost on the other fork: Denver led big by halftime, Harvey and the backups closed the game, and Dobbins sat on 61 yards the way he did in week 9, or the game stayed close and Denver threw because Surtain was out and LV's safeties were limited. Those two losses do not arrive together — a true blowout helps the Jeanty under and hurts Dobbins, a true coin-flip does the opposite — so the pair only cashes in the base 26-16.5 script. If that counter-case feels more likely than a controlled Denver lead, the Dobbins lean is the one to drop; the Jeanty under still has the run-defense numbers behind it.
